name: EDELWEISS germanium bolometer array
notes: The NbSi transition-edge sensor is operated at about 44 mK (arXiv:2211.04176: 'The TES is operated around 44 mK'; arXiv:2203.03993 gives the same working temperature). The cryostat base temperature and the operating temperatures of earlier detector generations (Ge-NTD sensors, EDELWEISS-I/II/III arrays) are not given by the sources consulted (checked 2026-10-25), and no official site could be reached for them.

placements.note: No source consulted (checked 2026-10-25) gives a start date for this placement; the start is left unknown.
placements.quote: operated underground at the Laboratoire Souterrain de Modane (LSM)

summary.plain: A block of ultra-pure germanium, cooled to near absolute zero deep under the French Alps, wired to catch both the tiny jolt of heat and the trickle of electric charge freed when a particle strikes an atom inside.
summary.technical: Germanium bolometer with combined ionization and phonon readout; the current sub-GeV programme instruments a 200 g crystal with an NbSi TES and Neganov-Trofimov-Luke phonon amplification, reaching a 30 eV analysis threshold and 4.46 eV electron-recoil resolution.

technology.quote: a massive (200g) germanium detector instrumented with a NbSi Transition Edge Sensor (TES)
technology.value: Cryogenic germanium bolometers reading both ionization (charge) and phonon (heat) signals; the current sub-GeV programme uses NbSi transition-edge sensors with Neganov-Trofimov-Luke phonon amplification
